Metrics available in shared_importance()

Source: R/metrics.R
as_metric.Rd

shared_importance() evaluates predictions with yardstick metrics. The metric argument accepts a built-in metric name or any yardstick metric function (class numeric_metric, class_metric, or prob_metric) whose direction is "maximize" or "minimize". The direction determines the sign convention: importance is +(full - reduced) for metrics to maximize and -(full - reduced) for metrics to minimize, so that a positive value always means that keeping the anchor feature predicts better.

Usage

as_metric(metric, task, label = NULL)

mse(data, truth, estimate, na_rm = TRUE, case_weights = NULL, ...)

Arguments

metric

A metric name or a yardstick metric function.

task

"regression" or "classification".

label

Optional display name for a metric passed as a function.

data, truth, estimate, na_rm, case_weights, ...

Standard yardstick metric arguments.

Value

as_metric() returns an object of class sharedimp_metric with elements name, direction, kind ("numeric", "class" or "prob"), and fn. mse is the yardstick-style metric function itself.

Details

Built-in names:

nametaskdirection
"mse" (default)regressionminimize
"rmse"regressionminimize
"mae"regressionminimize
"rsq"regressionmaximize
"mn_log_loss" (default)classificationminimize
"accuracy"classificationmaximize
"roc_auc"classificationmaximize

"mse" is the mean squared error, implemented as a yardstick metric because yardstick does not ship one. For binary tasks the first level of y is the event level of probability metrics; for multiclass tasks "roc_auc" uses the Hand-Till estimator (the yardstick default).

Examples

m <- as_metric("rmse", task = "regression")
m$direction
#> [1] "minimize"
m2 <- as_metric(yardstick::mae, task = "regression")
m2$name
#> [1] "custom metric"
mse(data.frame(t = c(1, 2, 3), e = c(1, 2, 5)), t, e)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 3
#>   .metric .estimator .estimate
#>   <chr>   <chr>          <dbl>
#> 1 mse     standard        1.33
